nodes.name: Molten-alkali synthesis
nodes.procedure: CoCl₂·6H₂O and K₂CO₃ were utilized as raw materials in a molten-alkali method. Typically, 1 g of K₂CO₃ and 20 mg of CoCl₂·6H₂O were homogeneously mixed via grinding in a mortar. Then, the resulting mixture was calcined in a tube furnace by heating it from room temperature to 860°C at a rate of 5°C per minute, holding at this temperature for 2 h, and then naturally cooling to room temperature. The product was then cleaned three times using ultrapure water, followed by freeze-drying, to yield the final LQNMP-Co₂O₃ catalyst.

nodes.characterization_summary: Nanosheet thickness estimated to be 0.9-1 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Additionally, the results of atomic force microscopy (AFM) further confirmed that the thickness of nanosheets was estimated to be 0.9-1 nm (Figure 1c).
The detailed morphological characteristics of LQNMP Co₂O₃ were illustrated in the transmission electron microscopy (TEM) image, which further confirmed the structure of ultrathin sheets (Figure 1d).

nodes.characterization_summary: Lattice planes of (01-10) and (10-11) with 120° angle, verifying highly crystalline structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) image of LQNMP-Co₂O₃ exhibited lattice planes of (01-10) and (10-11) with a 120° angle, verifying the highly crystalline structure...

nodes.characterization_summary: Co and O elements uniformly distributed in nanosheet; atomic ratio Co:O close to 2:3.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Co and O elements were uniformly distributed in the LQNMP-Co₂O₃ nanosheet layer... The elemental analysis results in Figure S4 suggest that the atomic ratio of Co and O is close to 2:3.

nodes.characterization_summary: Specific surface area ≈ 8.3 m²/g, pore sizes 40-50 nm, pore volume 0.02142 cm³/g, porosity 4.34%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The specific surface area of LQNMP-Co₂O₃ is approximately 8.3 m²/g with pore sizes mainly distributed between 40 and 50 nm. Additionally, the pore volume (V_pore) is 0.02142 cm³, and the total volume of the material (V_sample) is 0.4933 cm³. The porosity is calculated to be 4.34%.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co 2p: Co²⁺ (781.8/796.8 eV), Co³⁺ (779.8/794.8 eV), satellites (785.3/802.2 eV); Co²⁺/Co³⁺ = 36.04%; O 1s: O_vacancy (531.5 eV), O_adsorbed (532.8 eV), lattice Co-O (520.1 eV).
nodes.evidence_snippet: As depicted in Figure 2a, the Co 2p spectra of LQNMP-Co₂O₃ can be fitted into two separate peaks (Co 2p₃/₂ and Co 2p₁/₂) with two satellites at 785.3 and 802.2 eV, while the peaks at 796.8 and 781.8 eV are attributed to Co²⁺ and the peaks at 794.8 and 779.8 eV just represent Co³⁺... According to Figure 2b, the O 1s spectra of LQNMP-Co₂O₃ can be divided into three well-fitted peaks... oxygen vacancy (O-vacancy) at 531.5 eV, and lattice oxygen (Co-O) at 520.1 eV.

nodes.characterization_summary: Signal at g = 2.004 indicating rich oxygen vacancies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure S7, the LQNMP-Co₂O₃ exhibited an electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) signal at g = 2.004, indicating the rich oxygen vacancies within it...

nodes.characterization_summary: Significant agglomeration forming large granular particles with average diameter 5 μm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The SEM images of C-Co₃O₄ (Figure S5b) revealed significant agglomeration, forming large granular particles with an average diameter of 5 μm.

nodes.characterization_summary: Aggregates composed of particles ≈ 100 nm in size.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Meanwhile, C-CoO exhibited aggregates composed of particles that are approximately 100 nm in size (Figure S6b).

nodes.characterization_summary: Co²⁺/Co³⁺ atomic ratio 60.00%; exists entirely in divalent state for C-CoO.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Notably... the atomic ratio of Co²⁺/Co³⁺ for LQNMP-Co₂O₃ (36.04%, Figure 2a) is lower than that of C-Co₃O₄ (60.00%, Figure 2c)... In contrast, C-CoO exists entirely in the divalent state (Figure 2e).

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-durability test: no additional peaks, crystal structure preserved.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As depicted in Figure S17a, the XRD patterns revealed no additional peaks, indicating the preservation of the crystal structure.

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-durability test: Co and O peaks changed slightly, confirming good stability.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Additionally, XPS spectra of Co and O peaks were changed slightly, which confirms the good stability of the LQNMP-Co₂O₃ catalyst (Figure S18).
